constraints.claim_impact: Keep geometric outcomes in pixels or dimensionless relative quantities; do not claim instrument-traceable absolute position, reciprocal-space calibration, or instrumental uncertainty.
Do not interpret Gaussian amplitude or fitted volume as calibrated absolute LEED intensity or compare it as a calibrated intensity scale across acquisitions.
Do not attribute changes to a specified preparation state, contamination level, adsorbate exposure, or pressure history.

Use the Cu series as a recorded temperature-indexed positive control; do not claim kinetics, a calibrated thermal-expansion coefficient, a phase-transition temperature, or thermal-hysteresis attribution.

Treat Ag evidence as case-based behavior over recorded energy sequences; do not claim time-dependent scan kinetics, temperature-dependent Ag behavior, or a calibrated structural LEED I(V) interpretation.
Midpoint drift and apparatus-shadow behavior may remain diagnostics but must not be attributed to a specific physical component or generalized to other LEED systems.
Treat Scans A and B as two separately acquired case series under the tested measurement contract, not controlled population replicates.
The National Instruments IMAQ tag may identify the TIFF writer only; it cannot identify the camera or detector model.
